learning: Iteration 0 gave the best score (65.96) with max_error of 0.062 to 0.066 m. Iteration 1 changed several variables together and scored lower (53.33). The next race tests whether a shorter lookahead lowers max_error with the gain structure held fixed. If kd damping is now insufficient, the next step is a separate, single gain change.
notes: Geometry matches the Builder's isolated sensor-row test: iteration 0 chassis and 12 mm sensors on 12 mm pitch, with the sensor row moved from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.04 m. The controller is kept from iteration 0 so the race changes only one geometry variable.
rationale: The Builder's intent is a single-variable test. Iteration 0 (0.8 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch, sensors at y = 0.06 m) scored 65.96, the best so far. Every run in iterations 0 and 1 ended off track, and max_error sat at 0.062 to 0.066 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, while RMS stayed at 0.019 to 0.032 m. Iteration 1 changed four things at once and scored 53.33, so the Builder's lag hypothesis is worth isolating. Iteration 0 also shows high control_effort on the s-bend (1.45) and slalom (1.36), and steering oscillation of 0.11 to 0.16 on every track. Because this test is meant to isolate the sensor row, I keep the controller structure from iteration 0 (kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). Moving the sensors to y = 0.04 m shortens the lookahead, so the same kd may now damp less of the signal. I have no race evidence on this, so I do not change gains now. Any change in the next race can then be attributed to the geometry. Expected outcome, unverified: lower max_error if sensing lag is the cause, and a result that can be compared directly with iteration 0.
